context: Two architecture students planning a presentation on rammed earth as a building material

cues.t: Part 3. You will hear two architecture students, Laura and Finn, planning a presentation on rammed earth as a building material. First you have some time to look at questions 21 to 25.
Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 25.
Finn, can we plan the rammed earth presentation? It's only ten days away.
Sure. I was thinking we should begin by explaining how we came to choose the topic.
Wasn't it your trip to Morocco? You came back full of ideas.

No, that was afterwards. We'd already chosen it by then. What started it was that radio programme about the farmhouse in Wales. And remember, Dr Marsh was trying to persuade us to do recycled plastic instead.
That's right, she was. Okay. Then we need to set out the advantages. Everyone says rammed earth is cheap, because the soil is free.

The soil may be free, but the labour isn't. Ramming the walls by hand takes weeks, so it isn't cheap at all. And whether it looks good is a matter of taste. For me, the point that matters most is the way it keeps a building at an even temperature. The thick walls soak up heat during the day and give it back at night, so you hardly need heating or air conditioning.

Agreed, we'll lead with that. I'd like to say something about strength as well. I'd read that earth walls can last for centuries, so that didn't surprise me. What did surprise me was how much it depends on the soil. If there's too much clay in it, the walls crack as they dry, so the soil on every site has to be tested.
Yes, we should warn people about that. And then the difficulties. I suppose the wet climate here is the big one.

I don't think so. With a good roof and a stone base, rain isn't a problem. And you can always train builders to work with it. The real obstacle is that the building regulations here don't mention rammed earth at all. So you can't get a design approved, and nobody will insure it.
Good point. Now, how shall we divide it up?
I'll do the introduction. And since you did the laboratory work, perhaps you could explain the test results.
I'd rather you did the figures, to be honest. You explain numbers more clearly than I do. I'll describe the case studies. I've got all the photographs.
Fine by me.
Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 26 to 30.
Now listen and answer questions 26 to 30.
So tell me about the case studies. Which buildings have you got?

Five. The first is Riverbend School, in Kenya. What I like about it is that no construction company was involved. The parents and neighbours put it up themselves, without being paid, over two summers.
That's a good story. And the library?
Sanda Library. It's two storeys high, and two years after it opened there was a major earthquake. Concrete buildings nearby collapsed, and the library was still standing.
Impressive. What about the café you mentioned?

The Lotus Café. That one's a warning, really. To save money, the owners left out the stone base, and in the first winter the river flooded and soaked the bottom of the walls. Half of it had to be pulled down.
We should definitely include that. And the hostel?

Mountain View Hostel, in Austria. It looks wonderful, and it was finished on time. But the local soil had too much clay in it, so all the earth had to be brought in by lorry, and the final bill was almost double the original budget.
So it went well over budget. And the last one?
The Harbour Pavilion. It took twice as long to build as anyone expected. But last year it was given an international prize for design, which is probably why people have heard of it.
Great. That gives us a good mix of successes and failures.
That is the end of Part 3. You now have half a minute to check your answers.

items.stem: How did the students first become interested in rammed earth?

options.A: Finn visited an earth building abroad.
options.C: They heard a programme about it.

items.stem: What does Finn think is the greatest advantage of rammed earth?
What surprised Laura about the strength of rammed earth?

options.A: It can last for hundreds of years.
options.B: It depends on the type of soil.
options.C: It increases as the walls get older.

items.stem: According to Laura, the main barrier to building with rammed earth locally is
What will Finn do in the presentation?

groups.instruction: What does Finn say about each of the following buildings?
groups.limit: Choose FIVE answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–F, next to Questions 26–30.

options.B: It was built by unpaid local people.
options.C: It was finished ahead of schedule.

questions.explain:
答案是 C。Finn 說 What started it was that radio programme about the farmhouse in Wales。
同義轉換：radio programme ＝ a programme，heard 對應收音機。陷阱：A 是 Laura 的印象，但 Finn 說 that was afterwards，摩洛哥之行是選定題目之後的事；B 錯在老師其實希望他們做再生塑膠。
questions.quote: No, that was afterwards. We'd already chosen it by then. What started it was that radio programme about the farmhouse in Wales.

questions.explain:
答案是 A。Finn 說 the point that matters most is the way it keeps a building at an even temperature。
同義轉換：an even temperature ＝ temperatures stable。陷阱：B 是 Everyone says，但人工很貴，it isn't cheap at all；C 的外觀是 a matter of taste（見仁見智）。題目問 greatest advantage，對應 the point that matters most。
questions.quote: For me, the point that matters most is the way it keeps a building at an even temperature.

questions.explain:
答案是 B。Laura 說 What did surprise me was how much it depends on the soil，黏土太多牆就會裂。
陷阱：A 的「可以撐好幾百年」她早就讀過（last for centuries），that didn't surprise me；C 整段都沒提到。題目問 surprised，要分清楚「不意外」和「意外」的兩件事。
questions.quote: What did surprise me was how much it depends on the soil. If there's too much clay in it, the walls crack as they dry.

questions.explain:
答案是 A。Laura 說 The real obstacle is that the building regulations here don't mention rammed earth at all。
同義轉換：regulations don't mention it ＝ lack of official standards。陷阱：C 是 Finn 的猜測，被 Laura 否定（I don't think so）；B 錯在工人 you can always train。
questions.quote: The real obstacle is that the building regulations here don't mention rammed earth at all.

questions.explain:
答案是 C。Finn 說 I'll describe the case studies. I've got all the photographs。
陷阱：A 是 Laura 要做的；B 是 Laura 建議 Finn 做的，但他說 I'd rather you did the figures，把數據推回給 Laura。別人的建議不等於最後的決定。
questions.quote: I'd rather you did the figures, to be honest. You explain numbers more clearly than I do. I'll describe the case studies.

questions.explain:
答案是 B（由當地人無償興建）。Finn 說 The parents and neighbours put it up themselves, without being paid。
同義轉換：without being paid ＝ unpaid；parents and neighbours ＝ local people；put up ＝ build。
questions.quote: The parents and neighbours put it up themselves, without being paid, over two summers.

questions.explain:
答案是 F（撐過地震）。Finn 說大地震後 Concrete buildings nearby collapsed, and the library was still standing。
同義轉換：was still standing ＝ withstood。
questions.quote: Concrete buildings nearby collapsed, and the library was still standing.

questions.explain:
答案是 D（被水損壞）。Finn 說 the river flooded and soaked the bottom of the walls。
同義轉換：flooded、soaked ＝ damaged by water。陷阱：他提到 To save money，但這是省掉石頭底座的原因，不是 A（超出預算）。
questions.quote: To save money, the owners left out the stone base, and in the first winter the river flooded and soaked the bottom of the walls.

questions.explain:
答案是 A（超出預算）。Finn 說 the final bill was almost double the original budget，Laura 總結 So it went well over budget。
陷阱：it was finished on time 是「準時」完工，不是 C 的「提前」完工（ahead of schedule）。
questions.quote: so all the earth had to be brought in by lorry, and the final bill was almost double the original budget.

questions.explain:
答案是 E（獲得國際獎項）。Finn 說 last year it was given an international prize for design。
同義轉換：prize ＝ award。陷阱：It took twice as long to build 和 C（提前完工）正好相反，所以 C 是本題組沒用到的選項。
questions.quote: But last year it was given an international prize for design, which is probably why people have heard of it.
